phases.title: Phase 1: Kubernetes Basics
phases.description: Build confidence with the Kubernetes API, Pods, and declarative resources.

quests.title: Inspect the cluster
quests.description: Start by listing the nodes and namespaces available to you.
hints: Use kubectl get with a resource name.
quests.simulatedOutput:
NAME     STATUS   ROLES           AGE   VERSION
node-01  Ready    control-plane   42d   v1.29.4

NAME              STATUS   AGE
default           Active   42d
kube-system       Active   42d
k8s-lab           Active   2d

quests.title: Run a web Pod
quests.description: Create a small nginx Pod named web and let the scheduler place it.
hints: kubectl run creates a single Pod.
The expected shape is kubectl run web --image=nginx

quests.title: Describe the Pod
quests.description: Inspect scheduling, networking, and container details for web.
quests.simulatedOutput:
Name:             web
Namespace:        default
Status:            Running
Node:              node-01/10.0.0.21
IP:               10.244.0.12
Containers:
  nginx:
    Image:          nginx
    State:          Running
Events:
  Normal  Scheduled  12s  default-scheduler  Successfully assigned default/web to node-01

phases.title: Phase 2: Storage & Persistence
phases.description: Learn how StorageClasses, PersistentVolumes, and PVCs give workloads durable data.

quests.title: Inspect StorageClasses
quests.description: Discover the default storage class, then inspect its provisioner and binding mode.
hints: Use kubectl get sc to list classes.
Then use kubectl describe sc standard.
quests.simulatedOutput:
NAME                 PROVISIONER             RECLAIMPOLICY   VOLUMEBINDINGMODE      ALLOWVOLUMEEXPANSION   AGE
standard (default)   rancher.io/local-path   Delete          WaitForFirstConsumer   false                  42d

Name:            standard
IsDefaultClass:  Yes
Provisioner:     rancher.io/local-path
VolumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer

quests.title: Create a PersistentVolumeClaim
quests.description: Request 1Gi of durable storage and verify that the claim reaches Bound status.
hints: You can apply a manifest: kubectl apply -f pvc.yaml.
A command-line alternative is kubectl create -f pvc.yaml.
quests.simulatedOutput:
persistentvolumeclaim/app-data created

NAME       STATUS   VOLUME                                     CAPACITY   ACCESS MODES   STORAGECLASS   AGE
app-data   Bound    pvc-7c1a2d4e-9f40-4a1c-bc19-1a3f8f0c9c11   1Gi        RWO            standard       2s

quests.title: Mount a PVC to a Pod
quests.description: Inspect storage-pod and confirm that app-data is mounted at /var/lib/app.
hints: Look for Volumes and Mounts in the output.
quests.simulatedOutput:
Name:             storage-pod
Namespace:        default
Status:           Running
Containers:
  app:
    Image:          nginx:1.25
    Mounts:
      /var/lib/app from app-data (rw)
Volumes:
  app-data:
    Type:       PersistentVolumeClaim
    ClaimName:  app-data
    ReadOnly:   false
Events:
  Normal  SuccessfulAttachVolume  8s  kubelet  AttachVolume.Attach succeeded for volume app-data

quests.title: Troubleshoot a Pending PVC
quests.description: A claim is Pending because it requests a non-existent storage class. Diagnose it with describe, then fix the manifest by applying pvc-fixed.yaml.
hints: First inspect events with kubectl describe pvc stuck-data.
The repaired manifest uses storageClassName: standard.
quests.simulatedOutput:
Name:          stuck-data
Status:        Pending
StorageClass:  fast-ssd
Events:
  Warning  ProvisioningFailed  18s  persistentvolume-controller  storageclass.storage.k8s.io "fast-ssd" not found

# After applying pvc-fixed.yaml
persistentvolumeclaim/stuck-data configured
NAME         STATUS   VOLUME                                     CAPACITY   STORAGECLASS
stuck-data   Bound    pvc-3bfc9a1d-2d40-4c69-8c9d-4a3c1af8f921   2Gi        standard
